claims.text: Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variable friction and wear performance during sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
Depositing an adaptive nanocomposite coating will promote in situ formation of protective tribo-oxide films during sliding.
The proposed nanocomposite coating is stable at high temperature.
The coating can adapt its surface chemistry under sliding stress to form self-lubricating oxide layers.
During sliding in oxygen, the coating will react with oxygen to generate a thin, stable film of lubricious oxides.
The lubricious oxide film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
Minimizing direct metal contact through the oxide film will reduce friction and wear.
The nanocomposite structure will maintain the coating's mechanical integrity across room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanocomposite structure will maintain the coating's chemical integrity across room temperature to 800 °C.
Compared with unmodified CoCrFeNi, the coated material will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction at all tested temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C.
Compared with unmodified CoCrFeNi, the coated material will have a consistently lower wear rate at all tested temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating will make friction and wear less sensitive to temperature across the test range.
Stable lubricious films will form at both low and high test temperatures.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi shows increased friction at the temperature extremes.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi shows increased wear at the temperature extremes.
Coating performance depends on adhesion to the CoCrFeNi substrate.
Coating performance depends on thermal-expansion compatibility with the CoCrFeNi substrate.
